utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, may I invite you to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon to everyone. Before the Chamber gives an opportunity to you, Mr. Dutertre, to re-examine Professor Dunjic, I'd like to deliver one decision and give a statement on behalf of the Chamber. It's the reasons for the subpoena of Witness 28 and disposal of a motion filed on the 5th of March, 2007. These are the reasons -- these are the Chamber's reasons for the issuance of a subpoena to Witness 28 on the 12th of July, 2007, and we will also proceed to dispose of a Defence motion dating the 5th of March, 2007. First, as to the subpoena. Considering that, on the 4th of July, 2007, the Defence for Mr. Haradinaj objected to the issuance of a subpoena for Witness 28, and that the other two Defence teams joined that submission, the Chamber will now give its reasons for issuing the subpoena. We recall that the Prosecution filed its fifteenth application for issuance of a subpoena on the 20th of June, 2007, wherein it stated that Witness 28 was unwilling to come to The Hague to testify. The Defence objected to this application on three grounds; namely, that the anticipated evidence of Witness 28 would be of very limited assistance to the Chamber, that the witness is refusing to disclose her sources and her notebooks, and that parts of the evidence are inadmissible on various grounds. The Chamber was not persuaded that Witness 28's anticipated evidence would be of very limited assistance. The evidence satisfies the prima facie requirements of relevance for the issuing of a subpoena. The other arguments raised by the Defence relate to the reliability and the admission of the potential evidence, matters which are, in this case, more appropriately dealt with -- more appropriately addressed at the time of the witness' testimony. There remains a possibility that some or all of the problems raised by the Defence may be resolved at the time Witness 28 appears before the Chamber. Furthermore, most of the Defence objections to Witness 28's testimony relate only to some parts of the witness' proposed evidence, and there are other parts of it that are not challenged. It is for these reasons that the Chamber decided to grant the Prosecution's request to subpoena Witness 28. Finally, we note that similar objections raised by the Defence in relation to the subpoena are to be found in a partially undecided application on behalf of Mr. Haradinaj pursuant to Rule 89(D), filed on the 5th of March, 2007, to exclude the evidence of Witness 28. In light of the foregoing comments on the issuance of the subpoena, exclusion of the proposed evidence before hearing Witness 28 would be premature, and therefore the undecided part of the March motion relating to Witness 28 is denied. This concludes the Chamber's decision on these two matters. Then I'd like to give a statement on scheduling. The Chamber would like to inform the parties of the non-sitting days during the coming weeks. This will assist the parties in planning their time for the remainder of the Prosecution's case. We will continue to sit four days a week with Fridays as non-sitting days. Due to an unavailability of interpreters, we will also not be sitting on Monday, the 27th of August. Furthermore, we will not be sitting the week starting the 24th of September. Finally, as a reminder, the 12th and 24th of October are UN holidays which, of course, means that we will not be sitting those days. This concludes the Chamber's statement on scheduling. If there's no other urgent matter to be raised at this moment, I'd like to invite Madam Usher to escort the witness, Professor Dunjic, into the courtroom. [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Professor Dunjic. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony already prior to the recess, prior to the summer recess. Mr. Dutertre, are you ready to re-examine Professor Dunjic? Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor Dunjic, good afternoon. I'd like to show you the video again, a video which is dated the 9th of September, 1998. Given that we have an issue over the date, I think this is rather to do with the 8th of September, 1998. This video is Exhibit number P72. I would like to start showing the video at 5:46, and we shall finish off at 6:18. We can see both bodies floating in the concrete part of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the video, please. [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have this picture on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Professor, can you confirm that the top part of the body is covered in a red-coloured shirt?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: We are showing the video again. Can you confirm that the top part of the body is covered in a red-coloured shirt?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Can you confirm that there is something on the body's head, some material?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks as if at the back of the head there's a material or a part of tissue is something that I really cannot identify on this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. On pages 7227 and 7228 of the transcript, Mr. Emmerson quoted a part of the testimony of Zarko Bajcetic: "[In English] It has to be stressed that the two bodies which can be seen on the video footage recorded on the 8th of September cannot be seen any more on the video footage made on the 9th and 10th. One of the bodies is wearing a red shirt and the second one is wearing a blue one. The reason why those two bodies cannot be seen anymore on these dates, because the rain on the 8th of September caused the water to sweep both bodies downstream." [Interpretation] Having recalled this, Professor, I would like to show you the video which was shot on the 12th of September, 1998, in the second half of the afternoon, around 20 to 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This video is Exhibit number P452. The ERN number is VOOO-6012. I would like to show the part which starts at 14:11 and finishes off at 15:02.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 15:30. That's my mistake, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, apart from that, whether it was a translation error or a slip of the tongue, I take it that you wanted to refer to a video shot at the 12th of September rather than on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had mentioned the 12th of September, Your Honour, but I did make a mistake in the time clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would ask for purposes of clarification, because I'm assuming that Mr. Dutertre is going to ask questions concerning either the condition of the body or the colour of clothing, whether or not this testimony is being sought as fact witness testimony or expert witness testimony, because if it's being sought as fact witness testimony, I would be interposing an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand your objection already. At the same time, Mr. Guy-Smith, facts and opinion given by an expert usually are intertwined in one way or the another, so let's first wait and see what the questions are. But I do understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. There's been no foundation laid, then, with regard to a particular form of expertise. It may be attempted to be adduced. I'm sure the Chamber appreciates my concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I appreciate your concerns. Let's first hear what the questions are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes, Professor, this is my first question: At the beginning of the video we hear somebody saying: " ... In the best condition," and then at the end of the video [In English]" ... a corpulent person there is something thrown over its head." [Interpretation] I'm fully aware of the fact that this is not a top quality picture; but what do you think there is in the middle of the canyon, at the bottom of the canyon here, in the middle of the picture which you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I interpose the same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, what one sees is -- of course, the Chamber can see what is on the video, and colours can be seen by both experts and laypeople. So the only thing that -- it might be that on the basis of the experience of Professor Dunjic that he sees more than we can see. Sometimes if I look at an x-ray, I can't see what a doctor sees. So, therefore, there's no objection to your question, but would you please invite Professor Dunjic to explain how his special skills enable him to see more than we see. If he sees anything more, the problem, of course, is that Professor Dunjic doesn't know what we see. So let him explain what he sees and then the Chamber will consider whether he sees more than we see, and then we'll ask for an explanation on what makes him see more than we see. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm simply anxious that if this exercise is to be done with the suggestion that what we're looking at is the photograph that one -- the individual in the photograph that one sees in D43 or in the videotape, that Professor Dunjic be at the same time then invited to compare it to the photographs in situ of the two bodies that he has identified as being potential candidates for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this one of them? I have difficulties in knowing exactly now what we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. As I understand it from the line of questioning that Mr. Dutertre has been pursuing in respect of the former piece of video and this piece, he is inviting Professor Dunjic to make comparisons between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: His findings and what he sees.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- between what was seen in the first set -- the first excerpt of the video, that is to say, the body floating with the red hood on, and this piece of video. But the professor has already testified as to the two potential candidates for the individual in the red hood and we have photographs of those remains found in situ in the blue file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, does this give you sufficient guidance? Because until now the comparison led us in, I think it was, one or two cases where the professor said, I do -- I still do not exclude for the possibility that this is the same person as we saw -- as the floating bodies. Adding a third or fourth candidate, of course, I don't know whether it brings much. But please proceed and keep in mind that the whole exercise until now, and I think from both parties, cannot go any further than saying that we cannot exclude, which is something quite different from positively establishing that these are the same bodies. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. To my mind, this body had not been discussed, but we will see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: This is what the cameraman says and the person that is accompanying him, a body wearing something red. It's a bit difficult for you to answer because the quality of this picture is not very good, but overall can you tell us whether the way -- what I mean is what this body looks like, the degree of decomposition and the amount of flesh, is this consistent with the quantity of flesh and the degree of decomposition consistent with the body we saw wearing a red shirt in the canal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic, I'd like to split up that question. The first one being whether the picture you see is clear enough to form an opinion about the presence of soft tissue on this remains. And then the second question would be, if you can form an opinion about it, to describe it and compare it with what we saw of the two bodies floating in the concrete portion of the -- of the river. So would you please follow that order in answering the question put to you by Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The quality of the photograph, or, rather, this video, is quite unclear. I can confirm that this is a human body because one can note an extremity, the upper extremity, the head, the trunk, and two legs. The position of the body is, to me, unclear. I'm not sure whether the body's on the side, as it might be judging by the legs, and the upper part of the body seems to be leaning on a stone. Furthermore, one can see some light red and dark red. This could be clothing of that colour, but I can't ascertain that because this also could be decomposition and putrefaction changes of the skin. Thirdly, I cannot judge the degree of putrefaction on the basis of this photograph. If I were to compare this with the previous photograph made on the 9th of September in the canal, one cannot exclude the possibility because of the red colour that we see here and that we see on the photograph. But there's no other conclusions I can make on the basis of this clip. But it is certainly a human body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes, Professor, on page 7234 of the transcript, you said that there was no discovery of the bodies because there had been too much rain. I would like to show you the video which is dated the 13th of September, of the next day -- which was shot on the day, following the day we've just seen. ERN number VOOO-6012. More specifically I would like to show the part which starts at 19:11 and finishing at 20:30. Interpreter's note: transcript lines 20 to 23. That between the 13th and the 14th, there had been no discovery of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll stop there. I had mentioned the fact that this was Exhibit number P452.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Professor, this is my question. This video shows the current in the concrete part of the canal. On the 13th of September, 1998, according to you, what impact would this current have had on the 13th and the 14th, when there was no discovery of bodies, on bodies that still had softer tissues on them in the bottom of the canyon and that had not been blocked by any stones or caught in any foliage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This quantity of water and the speed with which the natural canal was being filled with water in the direction of the Radoniq Canal would certainly have moved the bodies that were unattached downstream, significantly downstream. And the soft tissues which are putrefied already would become even more subject to putrefaction and decomposition. And at the same time the bodies which are being moved or which are hitting a hard surface may suffer certain injuries, fractures and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you think that these bodies I have described with some soft tissue that have not been blocked by any stones or caught up in the foliage could have been carried into the lake -- could have drifted into the lake?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That is not a question which falls within this witness' expertise. If I could direct the Trial Chamber's attention to the reports that have been provided by the diving teams in this respect, and they are in the yellow binder, I think at tab 16. The matter is dealt with fully and it's dealt with by reference to those who examined the possibility that Mr. Dutertre is putting and excluded it. Would Your Honour just give me one moment. It should be 16 -- in the English, 16B --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've got a problem. We were told to bring the light grey binder, so -- yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall withdraw this question to gain time, given that we do have time constraints. I shall move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Professor --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to make the position absolutely clear, since the issue has been floated, there are two expert diving reports which exclude the possibility that any of these remains could have been washed into the lake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. That is 16A, 16B --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 16C and 16D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just looking at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because 16A and B is about the 12th of September, so it could not have fully explained what happened on the 13th. But I'm now looking at 16D --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Which is of the 16th of September, yes, and there are references made to heavy rainfalls.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the prepenultimate paragraph, after describing the rainfall, the team concluded that all the bodies found and any bodies that had made their way to the canal bed, either concrete or non-concrete part, under any type of circumstance could not have been carried into the lake regardless of the strength of the water current.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you consider the lieutenant who wrote that report to be more of an expert as someone who has often --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, more to the point, he is leading the diving team and is examining the delta upon which he bases that conclusion. This witness hasn't been anywhere near that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So both might have their flaws in forming an opinion on the matter. Let's not discuss it at this moment because Mr. Dutertre has withdrawn the question. Let's proceed. Mr. Dutertre, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm grateful to Mr. Emmerson to have relied on the forensic reports with such accuracy, and I believe that Professor Dunjic does have some knowledge as regards the floating of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Now, the search is resumed on the 15th of September. Professor Aleksandric told you about having found a body in the spot we saw on the video, in other words, on the canal bed, and the cameraman were saying about these bodies ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't know what the B/C/S translation of that question was like, but I think it's come out as an incomplete question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's been translated up until the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Now, when the searches resume on the 15th of September, did Professor Aleksandric tell you about the fact that he had found -- a body had been found in the spot that we see in the previous video in the canal bed about which the cameramen had said. Did Professor Aleksandric talk to you about having found a body?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, are you speaking about a day in September or in December, when this search was resumed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: 15th of September was the date that was quoted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer the question? Yes. Colonel Aleksandric and myself discussed everything that was happening in the canal and made notes about it in the form of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I would now like to show you this same video, which is Exhibit P452, VOO-6012, the part which starts at 18:10 and which finishes at 18:30. The date mentioned is that of the 13th of September.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Dutertre, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: We can clearly see cattle, a cow, floating in the concrete part of the canal. Did you see any cattle when you went to the canal on the 11th of September, where the bodies were lying along the canal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that in person. This was at the beginning, in the narrowest part of the canal. There were some cattle both alive and dead, mostly dead, mostly cows, that couldn't get out of the canal because the sides were very steep and concrete so that they were trapped there and they simply died.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You can see on the picture, to the right-hand side, on the left-hand side, we can see a wall which would prevent any cattle from falling at this particular -- in that particular spot of the canal, which is the concrete part of the canal. How can you explain that a cow could have been found in this particular spot?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again, I interpose the same question with regard to whether or not this is being offered as expert testimony or fact testimony. We have had no information whatsoever that Professor Dunjic has any expertise within the area of hydrology or the movement of water or the speed of water or the effect of -- the effect of the movement of water on any material that may be in a canal or slough or any other form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, before you answer this question, whether you have any explanation of what is said to be a cow ending up at this place, whether your field of expertise give you any skills, or whether on the basis of your experience in your field of expertise you could come with explanations for the positions of domestic animals in this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any expert knowledge in hydrology but I can explain it to you, because here on the image we see the lower half of this concrete canal, and in the upper part where I saw the animals while they were alive, that part is narrower, with sides that are not straight and there's earth all around. There's a road near that concrete canal. So they were able to walk down the canal but they couldn't leave the canal because the slopes were slanting. And this is 1 or 200 metres before that part, before what we can see on the image. So that that explains how the water was coming from that area and that everything in the canal was washed down towards the natural part of the canal and Lake Radoniq.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you'll do at this moment, Professor Dunjic, is to testify about facts you observed personally; that is that higher up in the canal, the situation was different from what we see here, where there are concrete walls, and you apply, may I say, human logic on it rather than your expertise --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- The Chamber will consider whether it has the same view or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't know whether Mr. Dutertre wants to pursue this line of questioning, but the Chamber -- and I'm sure he will recall that we have evidence from Faton Setah that a mass comparable to a human body at Luka e Epreme at the start of the canal all the way down to the delta section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you say that's not disputed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's certainly not disputed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, of course, now a human body is not the same weight or the same size as a cow, but I think human bodies are to be focused on rather than animals. Mr. Dutertre, you see, if this was what you were aiming at, then Mr. Emmerson, and I do not see any other counsel contradicting it, says that this is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I note that, Mr. President. Knowing that on the Prosecution side it's not on the whole part of the canal that it could move. The evidence given by Mr. Emmerson do not go the same way as the Prosecution's.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I'm now going to put to you another question which is about the bodies' custody. Mr. Guy-Smith asked whether you had received documents about the chain of custody concerning the bodies which were in the canal, and my question is the following: Once the bodies had been taken, marked, by the forensic team in the canal and taken to the trucks, during the transportation of these bodies to the Pastrik Hotel, was there a member of your team accompanying the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Jecmenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Still on page 7349, Mr. Guy-Smith asked you: [In English]" ... Bodies or when you were finished with the bodies, there was no chain of custody documentation that went along with those released, was there?" [Interpretation] My question is the following: Once the post mortem was performed, the bodies remained with their markings?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And also at the same time, after the post mortem was finished, the same markings and labels were placed in the bags that we brought them in from the spot and they were transferred to wooden caskets which were closed. They were closed in the prescribed manner, and on the lid of these caskets there was the same labelling, the same markings for the bodies that we used when we labelled them, when we carried out the autopsy and photographs. And this was photographed, too. Then afterwards the unidentified bodies were buried together in a single space in front of the cemetery in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Right. So to continue on your answer, were you yourself present when the identified or non-identified bodies were sealed in the coffin with the markings which were put on these coffins?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We all controlled it and I did myself, too; that the same labelling was placed on the coffin as was placed on the body itself. And not only on the lid of the coffin, because the coffin was buried, but the cross that is placed above ground in the place where the body and the coffin is buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to come back to something else, another subject, pages 17 through 30 of the transcript. You said you've seen body, R-18, in September 1998. In your statement, 92 ter, concerning this body, R-18, you indicate in paragraph 411 that there were animal bites visible, and you also add that the body was only removed on the 12th. And if I understand you rightly, and I'd like you to let me know about it, between the 12th and the -- the 11th and the 12th of September, this body was in open air, was left in open air?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, the bite marks which you found could have been inflicted between the 11th and the 12th of September, 1998? It can't be excluded as an hypothesis, can it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. You can't exclude it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, another topic linked to the decomposition. Yesterday at page 7347, Mr. Guy-Smith asked you whether a body could be skeletonised completely in a week. You answered inter alia that the body of a little child could skeletonise in three or four days. My question is the following: Professor, for an adult body, how much time is necessary for it to be completely skeletonised?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the circumstances and conditions and the state the body was in before, whether it was exposed to factors which accelerate decomposition, and so forth. So there are very different intervals. A body can be skeletonised at a very short space of time, for instance, let's say, 15 days, if some of these factors contributing to skeletonisation are very strong. Or three or four months and if you have other circumstances and conditions you can have partial skeletonisation; so it all depends. It's a wide range, especially when we're talking about the exposed part of the body, the extremities, the face, et cetera, the abdomen, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another matter concerning post mortem examinations and especially the hair which were examined at length by Mr. Guy-Smith. Page 7275 you confirm that you didn't do any microscopic examination of the hair found on the barbed wire, and my question is the following: For what reason did you not examine with a microscope the hair found when you were in Hotel Pastrik?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to stress something that I perhaps omitted to mention thus far. We worked under highly specific conditions. When I say"specific" I mean in the broader, narrower sense. In the broader sense for us, both on the spot, on site, and at the hotel. We had difficult working conditions, that is to say, we didn't have complete freedom of movement or communication, and so on and so forth, because it was very dangerous to move around without the security provided for us at the locality itself and to move around the hotel, in fact. On the other hand, in the hotel, or, rather, in the conditions we were working in- it was the garage of the Pastrik Hotel - we had makeshift conditions for on-site examinations. We couldn't even have a computer, let alone a microscope or anything else to perform more detailed analyses. Therefore, we concentrated on the basic autopsy findings; that is to say, we wanted to establish the cause of death, first and foremost, and to collect as many elements as possible in order to identify the bodies or body.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm now passing to other topics. You just mentioned identification. Precisely about identification, at page 7336 and 7337, Mr. Emmerson asked you questions about body R-3 in paragraph 236 of your interview, 92 ter. I will repeat that. Body R-3 was first identified by you as being the body of Adzija Seferaj and then as being Misin Berisha. In paragraph 226, you indicate there was a number of persons of family Berisha at Batajnica 1 and 2. My question is the following, Professor: Could you tell us that all the persons having the name Berisha in 1998 belonged to the same family and are related by blood?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I can't say. It's a large family bearing the same surname. Now, whether they're all related, I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Page 7353 of the transcript, Mr. Guy-Smith asked you whether in Madrid Dr. Alonso had told you about the fact that the samples for DNA analysis on the bodies at Hotel Pastrik had been putrefied, and completely putrefied possibly, rotten. I thought that the DNA results had not been contested by agreement between the parties. Is it absolutely excluded to get DNA with the means of science today, is it excluded that it's possible to take DNA samples when there is total putrification?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to give you a more complex answer to that question. When we took the samples, they had already been changed through putrification on site. Putrification had already set in in the locality. And as they were almost -- had spent almost two years in a fridge, there were additional putrification changes. We stored them that way. Now, when we took them to Madrid, we observed ourselves, and Mr. Alonso also said it would be very difficult. We realised that ourselves. Now, in answer to your question, what I can say is this: There is an organisation that helped us in the process of identification, the ICMP, and that organisation had the same problems with identification and establishing the DNA profile with putrefied, exhumed bones. There are certain procedures which I'm not very well-versed in, but they're used today in order to identify the DNA profile with such very much changed, contaminated samples, where a DNA profile is required.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Professor. I have two short questions to ask now concerning the identification of R-15 identified by you as being Milovan Vlahovic. Mr. Emmerson asked you about the information given by Rade Vlahovic. My question is the following: Did you personally speak to the person called Milovan Vlahovic, who is another relative of this person? The name was Milovan Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this you can see that I personally talked to Rade Vlahovic, who is the son, who reported the disappearance of his father Milan and Milka, his mother, nee Markovic. On the 19th of April, this was reported. They were last seen in 1998. And we conducted the interviews. Now, as to this Mr. Vlahovic, that is the piece of information about the callus on the rib, the scar on the rib.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Very well. And for Milovan Vlahovic, you remember having spoken to this person who was a relative of Milovan Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Vlahovic was born in 1967, it says here. He worked in the MUP of Djakovica. Somebody asked me about that yesterday, unless I'm very much mistaken. So he was an employee of the police force. But no, I haven't got any more notes as to which other relatives were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we play video P452, ERN 603, 26 of September, 1998, 6:50 to 7:06, and that will be my last topic. P452.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] This is Jeco's, what we're working on now. He's missing this one. Do we have one of those big bags because I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Professor, my question is: What is it about this video --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sorry, we have no French translation. The French wasn't being translated. If French interpreters could look at, because what has been said and what appears at the bottom of the video image, so if this is again played and translated into French in order to have a complete record.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] This is Jeco's, this what we're working on now. He's missing this one. Do we have one of those big bags because I ... Yes, yes, we have for sure. This part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be played again? I understand that the French interpreters are trying to do their utmost best, too. Let's play it once again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] This is Jeco's, this what we're working on now, he's missing this one. Do we have one of those big bags because I ... Yes, yes, we have for sure. This part. Part?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] And now write it like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic, could you tell us what this is about, this video?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the second part of the body which was labelled as RS-7, and they are in fact the two bodies that were found -- well, they found one-half first, the police found the first half, and as the second half was missing and I wanted to see the locality where the bodies were found because we weren't present there on the 20-something of September when we arrived for the second time to Djakovica, then with the investigating judge we went on site for him to show us where R-2, R-3, R-4, and R-5, the bodies labelled like that were found. And as the part of the body was missing, I walked around the area and quite by chance in some high grass, across some water, I happened to spy this body which was most probably taken off, dragged off, across the water by some larger animals, from the larger part of the body they had found initially.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see on the transcript that is R-2, R-3. I thought it Re-2, -3, -4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Professor, do we --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber noticed that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Professor, my last question: Should I understand that for that at least a part of the removal of the bodies Re-2 to -6, you were present?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was on location when this part of the body was found. Now, all the bodies labelled Re-2, -3, -4, -5, were found by policemen. After our departure from Djakovica and they provided security to President Milutinovic when he went to the canal to lay the flowers, the wreath of flowers where the bodies were found, and as they moved around this area, this broad area, they came across these bodies that were hidden in the bushes. And then the judge, Judge Gojkovic called us to come the very next day. So this took place on the second day of our arrival; not the first day of our arrival, but the second day, when we found that portion of the body we just saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: My question wasn't clear. Were you present, Professor, at least when this part of the body was removed, Re-6?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, but it may be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, and you can see that on the picture, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's a considerable degree of confusion creeping in as far as numbering is concern, because as I understand it, the witness' evidence in his 92 ter statement is that he was present when Re-7 was found, which is a body part, DNA-linked to Re-5, that had been found and recovered before, but that he was not present when Re-2, Re-3, Re-4, Re-5, or Re-6 were found and removed from the scene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, Mr. Emmerson explained that the discovery of a part of a body linked to numbers Re-7 and Re-5, rather than any other number, were dealt with in this video footage. Is that your recollection as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only do I recollect it, but that's what was recorded. So this part of the body, Your Honour, is the part that I found the day after my arrival. All the others, Re-2, Re-3, -4, -5, and -6, were found by the police and transferred to Djakovica to be dealt with. So when we arrived in Djakovica once again, those bodies were waiting for us over there. But I wanted to see where -- the location where they were found. And when we went on the following day, we found this part of the body that was incorporated into the Re-5 body, so we managed to link up the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This has been clarified. Thank you. Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify one matter, if I might. At page 20, line 4, Mr. Dutertre asked some questions of Professor Dunjic in respect of paragraph 226 of his 92 ter statement as to whether the Berishas he's referring to in that paragraph as having been removed from Batajnica 1 and 2 were members of the same family. I don't know if that's a matter of importance to deal with with the witness. But if it is, Your Honours have the grey file, which includes the details in the first tab of the Milutinovic indictment, and at 75(D), that is, paragraph 75, subparagraph (D), there is recorded there the allegation of a mass killing on the 26th of March of members of one family, the Berisha family, when Serbian forces attacked the Berisha family compound and later threw explosives into a cafe where individuals had been sheltering. And there was a list at schedule D to the indictment of the Berisha family members who met their deaths in that way, which included those recovered by Professor Dunjic at Batajnicas 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, is there any dispute about what Mr. Emmerson just said?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. What I think is not contested is the results of the genetic tests, so I was surprised that the question would be discussed, this question of Berisha family and of the genetic tests at paragraph 226 of the 92 ter statement. This was talked about by Mr. Emmerson yesterday and I wanted to cover the question, but I thought there was no problem because of the agreement about the identifications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that when questions were put to the witness about putrefied and -- putrefied samples and contamination, that it was primarily to establish that methods used were not solid, were not precise enough, rather than to contest the outcome of DNA analysis. Is that correctly understood? And I'm looking to you, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's correctly understood up to a point. Based upon the last information that we received shortly before the break concerning two specific bodies which, as I understand, were examined by the same laboratories using the same fashion, a couple of questions have now come up with regard to issues concerning DNA identification that beforehand had seemingly been resolved or were close to resolution. As a result of what happened with these -- the results that we received, and it's actually more than the results, what we finally received were, among other things, the electroferrogram, which indicated a number of what I would call anomalies, and I won't take it any further than that at this point, but a number of anomalies that require further inquiry before - at least as far as the Balaj team is concerned - we can easily agree to DNA results. They have to be satisfied. We are in the process, as hurriedly as we can, of taking care of that issue, and as a matter of fact over the break, it's one of the things that I was attending to. I, unfortunately, am not a scientist so I was dealing with those who were and taking my instructions from them. But for the fact that we'd received the information with regard to specific bodies and that's R-1 and R-12 and specifically the notes, the information that formed the basis of the ultimate conclusions, we would have been in a different position. But fortunately, the Prosecution gave us information which we can look at and have an intelligent appraisal of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's good. Is there any further need -- Mr. Guy-Smith, do I understand you well that you'd like the witness to remain available until after the break? Is Professor Dunjic to remain available?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No. At this point, with regard to issues concerning conclusions with regard to -- with regard to DNA, I believe that Professor Dunjic has given us all of the assistance that he can in that regard because we do know that the samples taken, and for whatever reasons they were contaminated and putrefied, is really of no other moment than how that would ultimately affect the results, conclusions, with regard to DNA. So I have no further questions with regard to that issue with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And on any other issue at this moment? Because Mr. Emmerson put some -- no, he even did not put questions to the witness. Any further need?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Not on our behalf either, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to be complete, briefly, I think from R-1 to R-12 are distinct from the matter of the samples which were putrefied and for the bodies in general, the DNA analysis or tests have not exactly the figure. But it's not only samples. There were several samples made on the same bodies, several parts of the body which were used. Therefore, this question of putrefaction of samples was not so fundamental as the Defence claims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not start commenting in the presence of a witness whether questions put to him were fundamental, yes or not. I do understand that there are no further questions to Professor Dunjic. I also understand that there's another matter about DNA analysis which is still discussed between the parties. And if that discussion leads to anything the Chamber should know, we'll hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm hoping for resolution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. What I would like to do, as a matter of fact, and although we're not necessarily need you for that, Professor Dunjic, perhaps you'd stay for a second because if there would be any confusion. Have the parties meanwhile received a list of exhibits introduced, most of them as annexes to the -- to the 92 ter -- redacted 92 ter statement of Professor Dunjic? The redacted statement is P618. And I have on my list sequentially numbered from P619 up to and including P817 which, if I'm not mistaken, are all annexes to the report of Professor Dunjic. Also sequential numbering although sometimes, for example, 53 is followed by 53 bis rather than directly by 54. Are there any objections against any of the annexes, the annexes listed and described on this list, I hope the Prosecution -- the Defence has received.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At the present moment, based upon the concerns previously voiced, there are a number of annexes which deal specifically with DNA reports. They are proposed exhibit numbers 746 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 774, 779, and 815. I'm double-checking to make sure that's all of them, and I believe that is. And all of those are DNA report conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do you object against admission of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this -- at this moment I do. If, after I've had a conversation with Mr. Dutertre and we can more fully discuss it, there may be a point where what we end up doing is withdraw the objection and make other arguments with regard to those specific reports. But that is something that can be handled relatively quickly, hopefully by the end of today's proceedings, at least to give the Chamber an indication of what our ultimate position may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So for the time being, any other objections? Then P618 -- yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, very briefly. I shall look into this as quickly as possible with Mr. Guy-Smith. I wanted to draw the Chamber's attention on the following fact: Some parts of the 92 ter statement and some of the annexes should perhaps be confidential. Yesterday we moved into private session because of a witness' name that could have potentially been uttered, so I shall try to identify as quickly as possible those exhibits that should be filed confidentially. ICMP, as a general rule, has in any case asked for all its reports to remain confidential. I forgot to mention this at the outset, but I hope it's never too late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we'll then do is we'll give a decision on admission into evidence of those exhibits not objected to and -- provisionally all under seal, and you, Mr. Dutertre, are invited to, within 24 hours -- within 48 hours, to provide a list on which you indicate which of these exhibits should remain under seal and we'll then decide that the others will be public. That means that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I just add one comment whilst we're discussing the 92 ter statement itself. There is a single sentence in the redacted statement which I think has been left in in error, because the substance of the information to which it then refers has been redacted. Now, I'm happy to discuss it with Mr. Dutertre outside court and to come to the Trial Chamber with an agreed position rather than taking time up now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's redaction rather than protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's redaction rather than protection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think we can proceed and we still could invite Mr. Dutertre, if a mistake has been made, to replace that one page by another page. But I'd like to proceed with the matter. Otherwise, our lists are getting longer and longer. That means that P618 up to and including P745 are admitted into evidence, provisionally under seal; that no decision -- that not admitted yet is P746; then P747 up to and including P762 are admitted into evidence, under seal provisionally; that not yet admitted is P763, so that remains marked for identification; then P764 up to and including P773 are admitted into evidence provisionally under seal; P774 remains marked for identification, no decision on admission yet been made; P775 up to and including P778 are admitted into evidence, provisionally under seal awaiting the list of Mr. Dutertre; P779 marked for identification are not admitted at this moment; P780, up to and including P814 is admitted into evidence, as said before, provisionally under seal; P815 remains marked for identification, no decision on admission yet made; P816 and P817 are admitted into evidence. Then, Professor Dunjic, after this exercise in administration, rather, but there are no further problems, it seems, this -- your testimony has been concluded by now. I'd like to thank you very much for -- not only for coming in July but also returning to us in August, completing your evidence, and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break until 10 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we turn for a moment into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. In respect of the witness which is now before the Chamber, at an earlier stage protective measures were granted. The Chamber was informed by the witness, that's you, Mr. Fazliu, that you do not wish any protective measures to be applied and therefore the Chamber has decided to lift the protective measures and proceed on that basis. Mr. Fazliu, now, before you give testimony, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I ask you to stand and Madam Usher will hand out to you the text of the solemn declaration. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will read the text I was given. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fazliu. Mr. Fazliu, you will first be examined by Mr. Di Fazio, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Fazliu, can you just confirm those details for me? You were born in Grabanica, Kline municipality on the 24th of September, 1961. You're married, you have three children. Are those details correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You graduated from the University of Djakovica, and between 1985 and 1994 you worked as a schoolteacher in the school in Grabanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And in 1994 you became the director of that school and you remained director of that school until at least May of 1998.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You're a member of the LDK and you are still, as we speak, in the LDK.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In -- sorry, you are the LDK representative for a collection of five villages, including Grabanica, Bokshiq, Qeskove, Kepuz, and Dollova; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: I was in that capacity until the spring of this year, but now, since I was elected member of the presidency of the LDK for Kline, someone else was appointed chairman of this branch covering the five branches.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And in 1998, in particular in May of 1998, did you -- were you chairman of those branches covering the five -- the five villages or branches?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: There was someone else. I was a member of the presidency of the subbranch responsible for five villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In 1998 did the LDK enjoy considerable popularity in your village of Grabanica?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. It was almost the only party that was set up and that was functioning, in addition to some small parties which had also seats in parliament, like the party of Mr. Demachi was. The remainder were all members of the LDK.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So the vast majority of households supported the LDK.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: In my village, I may say that each and every one supported the LDK. But this was the case also in other villages, with the exception of two families in Bokshiq which were represented in parliamentary parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did the LDK enjoy that sort of support in the other villages that I mentioned to you earlier, Bokshiq, Dollova, and so on?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, they did enjoy full support.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And the fact of your village of Grabanica being an LDK stronghold, was that well known in the wider area where you lived, in other words, throughout Klina municipality?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, until the situation deteriorated and violence started to be used by the Serb forces, and then the KLA appeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you for that. But my question was this: Did other villages in your area, in your wider area, and I'm talking about Klina municipality, know that Grabanica and the people who came from Grabanica were LDK supporters?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, certainly they did, because we were engaged in activities in all the villages of the Kline municipality, and we had the same programme all over these places.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thanks. In your village of Grabanica, was there a village guard in existence?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: The village guard started to be organised in 1990, from the 3rd September strike when the Albanian workers went on a strike on the 3rd of September, organised by Mr. Hajrullah Gorani who was the leader of the trade unions. From that time onwards, we organised a guard in the village. But I think the other villages too had their village guards. In Dollova, the situation was more problematic because the village was mixed up. There were also Serbs there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The village guard that you speak of in Grabanica - I'm really only interested in Grabanica - that continued in existence up until May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that village guard organised under the auspices, or organised by, the LDK?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, by the LDK. We were organised from the central level up to the grassroots. We had Anton Kola, the member of the presidency, representing Kosova, and we received all instructions from this person until 1992 or 1993, when he was forced to flee Kosova because of the fear of being arrested by the Serb forces after he was imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, earlier you mentioned the KLA. When did you first become aware of the existence of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: First we heard of it in groups and then at the meetings we had on a level of branch or subbranches. But for the first time it was in 1997, in Laushe, I think. After that there was no dilemma for anyone about its existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say you heard about it for the first time in 1997 in Laushe, what was your source of information? Was it personal intelligence or information that you had or was that something you learnt of through the media or other sources?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: We discussed these things in our group, but something that we heard on television and in the media. After that we were certain about its existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And when you say, "we discussed these things in our group," are you referring to your LDK party in Grabanica?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. Every time we held a meeting we discussed this issue and we had some kind of secret meetings in smaller groups. It was not that we discussed it openly, in broad groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the KLA ever establish a presence in your village of Grabanica?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, when that -- when that occurred.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: That occurred sometime in the first months of spring, maybe April or May. It was then, when the first groups from the village went to Albania for arms, to collect arms, in coordination with Jabllanice, with the headquarters of Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just clarify something -- a few things from that answer. You mean, I take it, April or May of 1998, first of all?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: I may say that from some notes I had taken at the time, even though most of them were burned and many years have passed and I may make some mistakes about the exact dates, but I think you are right, it was around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But I've got my year correct, haven't I, 1998, April or May?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. And you say that some groups went to Albania to collect arms in accordance with the headquarters of Jablanica. Is that the KLA headquarters of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. That was the only staff or headquarters, that of KLA, which was established in Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber how the KLA headquarters in Jablanica acted with these groups in -- just a minute. Allow me to finish the question, please. Excuse me. Can you tell the Trial Chamber how the KLA headquarters in Jablanica acted with groups in your village in order to get arms in Albania, how that came about.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: The Jabllanice headquarters organised talks in different villages to coordinate its work, and there were volunteers, young people who joined these groups to go and get arms to protect -- mainly to protect their villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did that occur in respect of Grabanica; namely, young people from Grabanica working with the KLA to go and collect weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, in the surrounding villages as well, with the exception of Dollova village that I mentioned earlier because of its position and the existence of Serb families there, because there were over 20 Serb policemen in Dollova.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there any representatives of the KLA living in Grabanica in April or May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were, and they were known by the village. They were recognised. We knew as a village that we had Sadri Berisha, and it was through his coordination that the first and the second groups went for arms. In one of the groups was also my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who appointed Sadri Berisha as KLA representative in Grabanica?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: He was appointed by the KLA staff in Jabllanice in cooperation with the village leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that the LDK village leadership?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: At the time when the Serb violence started on the 13th of May, with the attacks against Kepuz village and elsewhere, then it was impossible for the party to engage in its activities and we organised our activities in cooperation with the KLA. And there was a representative from every family when it was agreed for Sadri to be responsible for Grabanice, to be its representative.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The agreement for Sadri to be responsible for Grabanica, was that -- was that a decision taken by the villagers or was it a decision taken by the LDK representatives in Grabanica?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: It was a joint decision. As I said earlier, the LDK was in the village and it, of course, gave its approval for this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what was to be the role of the LDK village guard after this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: You mean the role of the village guard? In actual fact, all guards were part of the protective -- protection force, but they were not dressed in uniforms because at that time we didn't have uniforms. So from the outside you couldn't tell them. But they were willing to join the army and to defend the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, what I want you to do is to explain to the Trial Chamber, please, the role of the LDK organised village guard that had been in existence since 1990 and continued in existence up until May of 1998. What I want you to explain to the Trial Chamber is how that particular institution continued to operate following the appointment of a KLA representative. Who was in charge of it, in other words, the LDK or the KLA? Do you know? Or both?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: I already explained to you that from the moment that it was set up, we agreed on a platform of cooperation and on Sadri leading the village in its defence. Then Sadri had all the powers to organise the village defence, engaging all the youths who were willing to help him with whatever means they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who nominated Sadri for this position, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: I explained it. It was done with the agreement of the villagers of Grabanice in coordination with the KLA headquarters in Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm going to put the question to you this way: Whose idea was it for Sadri to occupy that position?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: I think that earlier Sadri had joined that movement, and in the past he was also one of the guards of the village together with some brothers of his, so nobody was against him being in that position. He had also completed his military service in the former Yugoslavian army. He had the necessary expertise to do that kind of job.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So Sadri had joined that movement, and I take it that's the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the KLA, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is -- do you know Lahi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, certainly, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. How to say it, how to put it. His uncle is a grand, grand-nephew of my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know his brother, Selman?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I used to go to high school for three years with him. From Jablanica he came and we walked to the high school together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And in May of 1998, you knew Mr. Brahimaj, Mr. Lahi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, certainly I do. Even earlier than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How well did you know him in May of 1998? What sort of relationship did you enjoy at that time?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Are you asking me only about 1998 or even before that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd just like you to give a succinct answer and explain to the Trial Chamber how well you knew the man, Mr. Lahi Brahimaj. Was he just a casual acquaintance? Did you know him quite well? Was he a very close friend? Try and comment and give the Trial Chamber an idea of what your relationship was.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: It was a time when it happened that he stayed with his uncle in the village and we might play together for a week or so. Then from 1992, when Jabllanice was isolated by the Serbian forces, they had a clash with the Serb forces, then after that our contacts were very rare, because the Jablanica inhabitants were not very free to move about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I take it, then, that you knew him quite well as a child, but that from 1992 you saw him less often. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I want you to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I want to ask some questions that I think require us to go into closed -- into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Fazliu, I want to ask you about an attack on Grabanica that occurred in May by Serb forces. I don't think that's in dispute. Firstly, can you tell the Trial Chamber if, indeed, Serb forces did attack the village of Grabanica, or the area in which the village is located, in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: As for the date, you're not talking about a specific date, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I'm talking about May of 1998. I'll suggest a date. I don't think there's any dispute about that. Around the 20th of May, 1998, did Serb forces launch an attack on Grabanica and the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. I can say yes. But on the 16th there were shots heard from the direction of Dollova. But Grabanica, yes, it was attacked on the evening of the 19th of May and all day on the 20th of May by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did villagers from Grabanica put up any resistance to this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: The villagers of Grabanica together with some members of the KLA remained there until they ran out of munition and then they were forced to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: These are the men of the village of Grabanica?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. Probably two or three families. There were one or two women, but most of them were men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And they offered what resistance they could to the Serb forces then?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. We did what we could, but we did not have heavy weapons. But we resisted up until the evening of the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you participate in that fighting?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Everybody who was there and people who were ready, they stayed there up until that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did there come a time when resistance had to be abandoned?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, but the Serbs -- after a Serb family left from Bokshiq, they thought that in Grabanice there were heavy forces and they did not dare to come to the village of Grabanica. And we carried on resisting up until the end of the 20th and we lost one person, Lezi, in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: My question was: Did the resistance to the Serb attack eventually stop or come to an end?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serb attack lasted all day and did not stop up until the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's the 20th; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the men from the village of Grabanica and the KLA representatives continue fighting after the 20th or did they leave the area?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: In the evening of the 20th everyone left the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Including yourself?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, me too. I left on the evening of the 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where were you intending to go?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: We had no intention of going anywhere. We only wanted to leave the village, probably to work towards Lugu i Baranit or towards Dushkaja. But we had no intended target, place, to go to, because I did not know where the rest of my family was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you leave the area in company with anyone?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who were you with?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: As I've said earlier, I was with Naser Lika and there were other co-villagers. But we were together up to Gllogjan and then we parted ways. Some went towards Lugu i Baranit and others went towards Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who is we?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Me and Naser. We continued towards Jabllanice. The rest went towards Baran. I'm talking about the villages of Grabanice and Bokshiq.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where did you end up, you and Naser Lika?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: We ended up in Zhabel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll continue asking you questions about this trip to Zabelj and I'll refer to Mr. Lika as your travelling companion. Did you and your travelling companion go through the village of Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: We passed through Gllogjan. The road passes through Gllogjan. It goes down towards the church and on the left-hand side to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the purposes of the geography, is this Gllogjan in the municipality of Peja?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes. Up to there it is the municipality of Peja, and that's from -- from the western part of Grabanice where the Gllogjan belonging to Peja is connected to our part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a map now and I'd like you to point out a number of villages, please, which we may talk about during the course of your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, can the witness be shown Exhibit D32, please. Yes, D32. And I'd like to focus in, I suppose, on the middle right-hand third of the -- of that image. You can see that there are circles around some of the villages. Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have a look at what you can see on the screen, witness, please. I'd like to -- and on the side of the screen there you have a little red pen, if the usher would just assist you. I just want to mark some of the villages that may come up in -- that may have been mentioned already. Some of these villages are clearly marked. We can see Grabanica that you've mentioned and also Zabelj also that you've mentioned. I wanted you to mark some of the other ones. Firstly, can you see the village of Bokshiq?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you just underline that with the pen on the screen. If you just underline it, it will come up.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the village of Dollova that you've mentioned, can you see that? And can you mark that, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you do the same with the village of Ceskovo, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you do the same with the village of Kepuz.

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And could you indicate -- I'll withdraw that question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'll tender that particular image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit number P884, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? No objections. Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've told us, you've mentioned in evidence that you were heading towards -- that you went to the village of Zabelj with your travelling companion. Why that particular village? Can you explain that to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: Probably before then I had -- I remember I've only been to Zhabel twice and I never stayed there, but it was Naser's idea or my travelling companion, as you called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If you wouldn't mind, let's refer to him as "travelling companion" for the time being. Where did you stay in Zabelj?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: We stayed at the house of Tal Zeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, before we get details of that, I want to ask you about your trip to Zabelj, just one feature of it. You said that you went through Gllogjan. Did you see anyone, any of your relatives in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: FADIL FAZLIU
utterances.text: I can't remember. There were many people from our village and the surrounding villages, but I can't remember whether I saw any relatives of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
